text: Good morning. Can we go over the September budget before I start work?
Sure. Rent and utilities are fixed at 1400, and we set aside 300 for groceries this month.
Good, that matches what I remember. Let's also plan the trip to the coast for next weekend.
I'll draft a two-day itinerary for the coast trip and check train times this evening.
Quick one: did the invoice from the printing company arrive yet?
Not yet. I'll flag it if it shows up before end of day.
Thanks. Also remind me to water the plants tonight.
Morning. I want to revisit the budget again -- I think the grocery number was too low.
You're right to double check. Let's bump the grocery line in the budget from 300 to 350 and keep everything else the same.
Good, let's go with 350. Write that down as final.
Noted -- the September budget now shows groceries at 350, rent and utilities unchanged at 1400.
Switching topics: how's the coast trip itinerary coming along?
Almost done. Saturday is the lighthouse and the harbor market, Sunday is the hiking trail before heading back.
That sounds perfect. Book the smaller of the two hotels we looked at.
One more budget question -- does 350 for groceries assume we eat out twice, like usual?
It does, same as last month's assumption. If that changes, the budget number should move with it.
Understood, leave it as is for now. Did the printing company invoice ever show up?
It arrived yesterday afternoon, actually -- I should have flagged it sooner. It's 85 for the flyers, due in two weeks.
No worries. Add the 85 as a pending expense, separate from the regular budget.
Done -- 85 logged as a pending expense for the printing invoice, due in two weeks.
